newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, large CDs turnover seen.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, large CDs turnover seen.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen deposit rate contract on TIFFE ended firmer on Wednesday, in line with an easing in cash Euroyen rates on the market's belief that interest rates would remain low for at least until the end of this year, traders said
Certificates of deposits (CDs) were actively traded in reaction to dealers' need to roll over maturing CDs in early October.
The three month cash Euroyen rate was quoted at 0.53-0.52 percent, down from Tuesday's 0.54-0.53 percent.

About 350 billion yen worth of the key three-month CDs was traded at 0.53 percent, 490 billion yen worth of two-month CDs was traded at 0.52 percent, and 340 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was traded at 0.51 percent.
The benchmark overnight call rate was actively traded at 0.50 percent, down from 0.51 percent on Tuesday.
Despite the firming in the call rate in the past few days, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from counteracting upward pressure on rates by supplying ample liquidity to the market.

"A less than accommodative stance by the BOJ implies that the central bank does not want the market to have what they call "excessive expectations" for easy credit," said a senior trader at a major brokerage firm.

The BOJ's concern that the market believes low rates will continue for some time appears to grown even stronger in the face of the recent weakening of the yen which would put downward pressure on the yen's exchange rate, he said.
However, the market consensus is that the BOJ is unlikely to tighten before the end of this year, he added.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected 100 billion yen into the market, which had a projected shortfall of 100 billion yen, at its regular operation at 0020 GMT.
